text:
tara_support: FYI customer reported repeated 429/503s from our hosted API when using python SDK 0.9.3. They said retries created duplicate resources on 'create' calls. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-1987

liam_eng: thanks, can you paste their snippet + logs? is this happening on burst traffic or steady state?

tara_support: pasted minimal repro below from the customer. they call client.create_widget(...) in a loop. SDK shows retries, but server logs show duplicate creates (no idempotency token on their side). They said it used to be fine on 0.9.2.

---begin snippet---
# customer_repro.py
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=\"REDACTED\")
for i in range(3):
    resp = client.widgets.create({
        \"name\": f\"test-{i}\"
    })
    print(resp.id)

# logs from customer's run
# 2024-12-02T14:10:21Z - INFO - request id=abc123 status=429 retrying attempt=1
# 2024-12-02T14:10:22Z - INFO - request id=abc123 status=200 created id=wid-001
# 2024-12-02T14:10:23Z - INFO - request id=def456 status=429 retrying attempt=1
# 2024-12-02T14:10:24Z - INFO - request id=def456 status=200 created id=wid-002
# result: customer saw 6 widgets instead of 3
---end snippet---

maria_sre: interesting. 429/503 should be retried by the SDK, but create endpoints must be idempotent or require an idempotency token. Did the SDK change idempotency rules between 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3?

liam_eng: short answer: yes. there was a change in retry/backoff handling in 0.9.3. The SDK started treating 429 as a global retriable regardless of method idempotency in one internal refactor. Also default jitter was unintentionally set to 'none' which can make retries line up.

tara_support: customer expects either 1) no unsafe retries for non-idempotent calls, or 2) clearer docs + guidance to pass idempotency_token.

liam_eng: noted. immediate mitigation: instruct customer to pin sdk to 0.9.2 or explicitly set retry config and idempotency token. Example workaround: 

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED", retry_config={
    "max_attempts": 4,
    "backoff_base": 0.6,
    "max_backoff": 15,
    "retry_on": ["429", "503"],
    "jitter": "full"
})
# when creating resources, include an idempotency key
client.widgets.create({"name": "test"}, idempotency_key="uuid-1234")
```
liam_eng: that will avoid duplicate creates and spread retries. I'll open an internal bug and link a PR.

ci-bot: New issue created -> INF-SDK-742 by liam_eng: "python sdk: 0.9.3 retry logic wrongly retries non-idempotent calls + jitter default regression"

liam_eng: investigation notes: problem lives in retryer.py where _should_retry(response) always returned True for 429. it previously gated on method type and on presence of idempotency key. PR will restore that check and make jitter default to 'full'. Also adding unit tests for create/update/delete endpoints.

maria_sre: can you add a smoke test in staging that does high-concurrency create calls with deliberate 429 to verify no duplicates? also add a tracing tag so we can correlate retries.

liam_eng: yep. will add an e2e in infra-tests and a flag in the console to enable request-level idempotency enforcement for hosted customers while we roll the fix.

tara_support: customer is on a tight timeline. I've sent them the pin + workaround + ask to add idempotency keys. I've also opened support escalation CS-1987 and linked INF-SDK-742. I'll update them when the PR is merged.

liam_eng: timeline: patch branch up in ~2 hours, review + CI ~4hrs, deploy to staging same day, canary to prod next day if tests pass. assigning to eng-sdk triage.

maria_sre: FYI add a short-term rate-limit smoothing rule on the gateway to avoid thundering retry storms if jitter isn't applied client-side.

tara_support: thanks all. tagging @liam_eng for follow-up to customer. :thumbsup:
